reconcile.note: Gill notes the call in Genesis 12:1 named no destination, so Abram's ignorance was at the call itself, before Genesis 12:5 shows him en route with Canaan as his known goal.

discrepancy.note: Colenso traces the clash to two spliced sources: E has Abram purposely bound for Canaan, J has him leaving by command not knowing his destination.

quotes.text: Abram migrates from Charran proprlo motu, with the express intention of 'going to the land of Canaan,' xii.5 … as the apostle Kiys, * not knowing whither he went,' IIeb.xi.8.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), Critical Analysis of Genesis, sec. 62, on Genesis 12:5 and Hebrews 11:8.

sides.snippet: they went forth to go into the land of Canaan. Into the land of Canaan they came.
sides.verseText: Abram took Sarai his wife, Lot his brother's son, all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls who they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan. Into the land of Canaan they came.

sides.snippet: He went out, not knowing where he went.
sides.verseText: By faith, Abraham, when he was called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance. He went out, not knowing where he went.
